y: the 25th letter of the Roman alphabet
yahweh: a name for the God of the Old Testament as transliterated from the Hebrew consonants YHVH
yale: English philanthropist who made contributions to a college in Connecticut that was renamed in his honor (1649-1721)
yankee: an American who lives in the North (especially during the American Civil War)
used by Southerners for an inhabitant of a northern state in the United States (especially a Union soldier)
yelling: uttering a loud inarticulate cry as of pain or excitement
yellowstone: a tributary of the Missouri River that flows through the Yellowstone National Park
yelping: a sharp high-pitched cry (especially by a dog)
yemen: a republic on the southwestern shores of the Arabian Peninsula on the Indian Ocean
yemeni: a native or inhabitant of Yemen
of or relating to or characteristic of Yemen or its inhabitants
yiddish: a dialect of High German including some Hebrew and other words
yorkshire: a former large county in northern England
yoruba: a member of a West African people living chiefly in southwestern Nigeria
yosemite: a series of waterfalls in Yosemite National Park in California
yr: a period of time containing 365 (or 366) days
yugoslavia: a former country of southeastern Europe bordering the Adriatic Sea
yugoslavian: of or relating to or characteristic of the former country of Yugoslavia or its people or languages
yukon: a North American river that flows westward from the Yukon Territory through central Alaska to the Bering Sea
yuppies: a young upwardly mobile professional individual
